---
title: "Interactive NHL Shot Map"
description: >
  Turn the Stanley Cup clincher's shot map into a web chart: hover a shot for
  the shooter, period, time, shot type and result, hover a shooter to light up
  all of his shots, and keep each team's logo and score beside its end.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 96
)
```

**The brief:** the recap page for the Stanley Cup clincher already carries the
[NHL Shot Map](recipe-nhl-shot-map.html) image. The web version should let a
reader point at any shot and see who took it, when, what kind of shot it was and
how it ended, with the goals easy to find and each team's logo at the end it
attacks. The data is the same SportsDataverse NHL release through fastRhockey;
`sdv_surface()` draws the rink, and ggiraph makes the ggplot interactive without
losing the rink or the logos.

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(ggiraph)

season <- 2026 # the 2025-26 season: NHL seasons are named by the year they end
cup_final <- 2025030416 # Stanley Cup Final, Game 6
```

## 1. Get the data

The same two loaders as the static recipe: `load_nhl_pbp()` for the season's
play-by-play and `load_nhl_schedule()` for the final score. This time each shot
keeps three more columns for the hover: the shot type (`secondary_type`), the
strength state and the distance.

```{r data}
pbp <- fastRhockey::load_nhl_pbp(season)
schedule <- fastRhockey::load_nhl_schedule(season)

game <- filter(schedule, game_id == cup_final)

shots <- pbp |>
  filter(game_id == cup_final, event_type %in% c("SHOT", "MISSED_SHOT", "GOAL")) |>
  transmute(
    event_type, period, period_time,
    team = event_team_abbr, shooter = event_player_1_name,
    shot_type = coalesce(secondary_type, "unknown"),
    strength_state, shot_distance,
    x_fixed, y_fixed, xg
  ) |>
  mutate(
    result = recode(event_type, SHOT = "Saved", MISSED_SHOT = "Missed", GOAL = "Goal"),
    id = row_number(),
    xg_label = if_else(is.na(xg), "xG not recorded", sprintf("xG %.2f", xg)),
    dot_size = coalesce(xg, min(xg, na.rm = TRUE)) # a shot without xG draws at the smallest size
  )
sprintf("%s %d at %s %d", game$away_team_abbr, game$away_score, game$home_team_abbr, game$home_score)
count(shots, team, result)
sum(is.na(shots$xg))
```

The page embeds one row per shot, about a hundred rows, so it stays light. One
saved shot has no expected-goals value in the release; it stays on the map at
the smallest dot size, and its tooltip says so.
Blocked shots are left out, as in the static recipe: the feed records where a
blocked shot was blocked, not where it was taken.

The rink is the heavy part. `sdv_surface()` draws it with 'sportyR', whose
curves (the corners, the circles, the creases) are traced with over 120,000
points, many of them repeats a hundredth of a foot apart. A static PNG doesn't
care, but `girafe()` writes every point into the page, about 1.6 MB per chart.
Dropping each point that rounds to the same tenth of a foot as the one before it
keeps about one in six and leaves the drawing unchanged:

```{r thin}
thin_rink <- function(rink) {
  rink$layers <- lapply(rink$layers, function(layer) {
    d <- layer$data
    if (is.data.frame(d) && all(c("x", "y") %in% names(d))) {
      key <- paste(round(d$x, 1), round(d$y, 1))
      layer$data <- d[c(TRUE, key[-1] != key[-length(key)]), ]
    }
    layer
  })
  rink
}

rink_points <- function(rink) sum(vapply(rink$layers, function(l) NROW(l$data), 1L))
c(before = rink_points(sdv_surface("nhl")), after = rink_points(thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl"))))
```

## 2. A tooltip on every shot

`geom_point_interactive()` is `geom_point()` with three more aesthetics:
`tooltip` (the HTML shown on hover), `data_id` (which points light up together)
and `onclick`. The tooltip below names the shooter and his team, the period and
time, the shot type and strength, and how the shot ended. The thinned
`sdv_surface("nhl")` puts the shots on a rink with the home team shooting right,
and `girafe()` renders the whole ggplot as an SVG.

```{r tooltips, fig.alt = "An interactive NHL rink with the Stanley Cup clincher's unblocked shots as team-colored dots; hovering a dot shows the shooter, period, time, shot type and result."}
shots <- mutate(
  shots,
  tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b> (%s)<br>Period %d, %s<br>%s shot, %s, %.0f ft<br>%s &middot; %s",
    shooter, team, period, period_time,
    tools::toTitleCase(shot_type), strength_state, shot_distance, result, xg_label
  )
)

p_tips <- thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl")) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = id),
    data = shots, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_color_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, guide = "none")

girafe(ggobj = p_tips, width_svg = 7, height_svg = 3.4)
```

Every dot answers on hover, but a goal still looks like any other shot, and
hovering one dot lights up only that dot.

## 3. Goals that stand out, shooters that light up

Three changes. Misses become open rings, saved shots stay filled dots, and goals
become large black-ringed dots drawn last so they sit on top. `data_id` is now
the shooter, so hovering a shot lights up every shot that player took; the
`opts_hover_inv()` option fades everything else. A click keeps a shooter
selected (`opts_selection()`), for comparing where two players shot from.

```{r goals, fig.alt = "The interactive shot map with saved shots as filled dots, misses as open rings and the goals as large black-ringed dots; hovering a shot highlights every shot by the same player and fades the rest."}
draw_shots <- function(...) {
  thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl", ...)) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Saved"), alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Missed"), shape = 1, stroke = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Goal"), shape = 21, size = 6.5, color = "black", stroke = 1.2
    ) +
    scale_color_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, guide = "none")
}

shot_opts <- list(
  opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;color:black;padding:6px;border-radius:6px;font-size:12px;"),
  opts_hover(css = "stroke:black;stroke-width:1.5px;"),
  opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.15;"),
  opts_selection(type = "single", css = "stroke:black;stroke-width:2px;")
)

girafe(ggobj = draw_shots(), width_svg = 7, height_svg = 3.4, options = shot_opts)
```

## 4. Logos, score and headline

Each team gets its logo, score and shots on goal past the boards on the side it
attacks, as in the static recipe. `geom_sdv_logos_interactive()` is
`geom_sdv_logos()` with a hover target over each logo, so the logo gets its own
tooltip: the full team name and the shot totals. Its `data_id` is the team, which
doesn't match any shooter, so hovering a logo highlights only that logo.

```{r story, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "The finished interactive shot map: the clincher's unblocked shots on a rink in team colors, each team's logo, score and shots on goal beside the end it attacks, and a headline; logos and shots show details on hover."}
club_names <- sdv_teams("nhl") |> select(team_abbr = abbr, team_name = name)
scoreboard <- tibble(
  team = c(game$away_team_abbr, game$home_team_abbr),
  x = c(-122, 122), # outside the boards, on the side each team attacks
  score = c(game$away_score, game$home_score)
) |>
  left_join(
    summarise(shots, sog = sum(result != "Missed"), attempts = n(), xg = sum(xg, na.rm = TRUE), .by = team),
    by = "team"
  ) |>
  left_join(club_names, by = c("team" = "team_abbr")) |>
  mutate(tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b><br>%d goals, %d shots on goal<br>%d unblocked attempts, %.1f xG",
    team_name, score, sog, attempts, xg
  ))
winner <- slice_max(scoreboard, score, n = 1)
loser <- slice_min(scoreboard, score, n = 1)

shot_map <- function() {
  draw_shots(xlims = c(-142, 142)) +
    geom_sdv_logos_interactive(
      aes(x = x, y = 14, team = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
      data = scoreboard, league = "nhl", height = 0.2, hover_size = 14
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = -8, label = score), data = scoreboard, size = 11, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = x, y = -21, label = paste(sog, "shots\non goal")),
      data = scoreboard, size = 2.7, color = "grey40", lineheight = 0.9
    ) +
    labs(
      title = sprintf(
        "The %s won the Stanley Cup, %d-%d in Game 6",
        winner$team_name, winner$score, loser$score
      ),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "Every unblocked shot. %s shoots left, %s right. Dots: saved; rings: missed; large black-ringed dots: goals; size: expected goals.",
        game$away_team_abbr, game$home_team_abbr
      ),
      caption = "Data: NHL via fastRhockey  |  Chart: sdvplotR"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, margin = margin(b = 3)),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(color = "grey40", size = 8.5, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey45", size = 7),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 12, 6, 12),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    )
}

shot_widget <- girafe(ggobj = shot_map(), width_svg = 8, height_svg = 4.5, options = shot_opts)
shot_widget
```

The two logos are embedded in the SVG, so the chart needs no network once the
page has loaded.

## 5. Share it

`htmlwidgets::saveWidget()` writes the widget to one HTML file.
`selfcontained = TRUE` inlines ggiraph's JavaScript, so the file opens anywhere
with no folder beside it (it needs pandoc, which ships with RStudio).

```{r save-html}
out_dir <- tempfile("sdvplotR-recipe-") # where the file goes; use your own folder
dir.create(out_dir)
html <- file.path(out_dir, "nhl_shot_map.html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(shot_widget, html, selfcontained = TRUE)
round(file.size(html) / 1024) # kilobytes
```

## 6. A static version

The same plot without `girafe()` is an ordinary ggplot, so a social post or a
PDF gets the matching image: outside `girafe()` the `_interactive` layers draw
as plain points and logos, and the hover targets stay invisible. `ggsave()` it
as in the
[NHL Shot Map](recipe-nhl-shot-map.html) recipe.

```{r export, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "The static version of the Stanley Cup clincher shot map: unblocked shots on a rink in team colors, saved shots filled, misses as rings, goals as large black-ringed dots, with each team's logo, score and shots on goal beside its end."}
shot_map()
```
